label: Putnam 1967, Psychological Predicates (The Nature of Mental States)
why_relevant: Named-only in the manifest. The founding statement both Block papers target and every later work inherits; two paginations are in play and neither is canonical here

label: Bechtel & Mundale 1999, Multiple realizability revisited
why_relevant: Named-only in the manifest. The standard challenge to multiple realizability, which every reviewed work assumes; its absence leaves that premise unopposed in this corpus

label: Searle 1990, Is the brain's mind a computer program?
why_relevant: Named-only in the manifest. The compressed three-axiom restatement and the source of the wall-runs-WordStar claim that Chalmers 1996 answers

label: Schneider 2019, Artificial You: AI and the Future of Your Mind
why_relevant: Named-only in the manifest. Source of the AI Consciousness Test that Chalmers, Birch, Butlin et al. and Long et al. all assess; leaves a 16-year gap after Bostrom 2003

label: Thompson 2007, Mind in Life
why_relevant: Named-only in the manifest. The hub cited by all three biological works for continuity between life and mind; the highest-value single addition to this corpus

label: Putnam 1988, Representation and Reality (appendix, pp. 120-25)
why_relevant: The universal-realization argument itself. Reconstructed here only from Chalmers 1996 section 2; the corpus contains its critics, not the source

label: Searle 1992, The Rediscovery of the Mind
why_relevant: Contains the fading-qualia passage (pp. 66-67) that Chalmers 1995 quotes and answers, and the observer-relativity claims Shagrir contests

label: Egan 1991-1995, the function-theoretic view of computational content
why_relevant: The non-semantic, purely mathematical account of Marr's computational level; the direct target of Sprevak's individuation argument

label: Marr 1982, Vision
why_relevant: Read three incompatible ways inside this corpus; the disagreement about what Marr's computational level shows is itself part of the field's history

label: McCulloch & Pitts 1943, A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity
why_relevant: The origin of digital computationalism about the brain, and the source of the two assumptions Piccinini & Bahar show were never empirically supported

label: von Neumann 1951 and 1958, on neural nets and the computer-and-brain analogy
why_relevant: The route by which pancomputationalism entered the literature, and the source of the spike-rates-as-digits proposal reported as still unsolved

label: Block 1981, Psychologism and Behaviorism (the giant lookup table)
why_relevant: The standalone Blockhead paper; the held 1978 reprint contains the list-searcher at pp. 281-282, but the argument's canonical home is not in this corpus

label: Shoemaker 1975 and 1982, Functionalism and Qualia; The Inverted Spectrum
why_relevant: The argument that absent qualia are logically impossible, and the inverted-spectrum statement Chalmers answers; both known here only through citing papers

label: Lewis 1972 and Armstrong 1968, causal-role analyses of mental terms
why_relevant: The platitude and causal-role machinery Chalmers leans on for psychological properties and Block attacks with paralytics and brains in bottles

label: Haimovici 2013 and Dewhurst 2016, on mechanistic and physical-level individuation
why_relevant: The dilemma Coelho Mollo 2018 sets out to dissolve, and the physical-level proposal he rejects; both reconstructed only from that paper

label: Piccinini 2008 and 2015, Computation without representation; Physical Computation
why_relevant: The book-length mechanistic account and the anti-semantic paper; the held 2010 and 2013 papers are its sketch and its application

label: Oizumi, Albantakis & Tononi 2014, IIT 3.0
why_relevant: The formal statement the unfolding argument actually attacks, and the source of the Phi-additivity rule its construction uses

label: Lamme 2006 and 2010, recurrent processing theory
why_relevant: The second causal-structure theory the unfolding argument targets, and the source of Butlin et al.'s RPT indicators; represented here only second-hand

label: Baars 1988 and Dehaene 2014, global workspace statements
why_relevant: The theory statements that several reviewed works actually cite when they say 'global workspace'; the held Dehaene et al. 2017 is a later and narrower paper

label: Aaronson 2014 and Tononi 2014, the unconscious-expander exchange
why_relevant: Supplies the Phi-increasing devices that make Doerig et al.'s construction concrete; the exchange itself is not held

label: Kleiner 2020; Tsuchiya, Andrillon & Haun 2019, replies to the unfolding argument
why_relevant: The published defences of causal-structure theories. Their absence is why the testability debate reads as one-sided in this corpus

label: Maturana & Varela 1980, Autopoiesis and Cognition
why_relevant: The source of autopoiesis, the concept doing the heaviest lifting in Seth's positive case; known here only through Seth's summary

label: Hinton 2022 and Ororbia & Friston 2023, mortal computation
why_relevant: The argument against substrate flexibility from inside computationalism, which Seth says he finds the most provocative; not held

label: Barnett & Seth 2023; Rosas et al. 2024, causal and informational closure measures
why_relevant: The only proposal in the corpus that could measure how far a system's dynamics can be abstracted from its substrate; the measures themselves are not held

label: Cao 2022, generative entrenchment in evolved mental function
why_relevant: One of the three plausibility arguments against neural replacement (nitric oxide diffusion; homeostatic spiking); reconstructed only from Seth 2025

label: Harnad 1990, The Symbol Grounding Problem
why_relevant: The problem the Vector Grounding Problem restates, and the bridge from the Chinese Room to the language-model debate

label: Bender & Koller 2020, Climbing towards NLU (the Octopus Test)
why_relevant: The strongest case against grounding in text-trained systems; appears here only inside the papers that answer it

label: Metzinger 2021, a moratorium on synthetic phenomenology
why_relevant: The most restrictive policy proposal in the debate; assessed by Birch, Butlin et al. and Seth but never stated in its own words here

label: Birch 2024, The Edge of Sentience (the book)
why_relevant: The corpus holds the published precis, not the book; claims about how the framework is argued cannot be checked from the precis alone

label: Millière & Buckner, A Philosophical Introduction to Language Models, Part II
why_relevant: The companion paper reserved for interpretability methods and for consciousness, which Part I defers by design

label: Chalmers 1996, The Conscious Mind
why_relevant: The book whose views the 2011 footnote to A Computational Foundation was added to square with; the footnote is why sufficiency there is nomological, not metaphysical

label: Barnes 1991; Klein 2008, 2012, 2013, 2015; Bishop 2009a,b; Bartlett 2012
why_relevant: The entire reply literature on Olympia, mapped by Klein but not held. Bartlett 2012 is described as the existing survey, 'albeit in a Maudlin-sympathetic way'

label: Fekete & Edelman 2011, on whether inactive elements contribute to experience
why_relevant: The named dissent from the premise that experience supervenes on what a brain actually does, aimed at integrated information theory; reported only via Klein

label: Sprevak 2007 and Pylyshyn 1984, on program portability and architecture
why_relevant: The source of the claim that what programs a machine can run depends on its architecture - the hinge of Klein's reformulation, and cited by Butlin et al. on levels

label: Michel & Lau 2021; Wiese 2024; Shiller 2024; Arvan & Maley 2022
why_relevant: Recent restrictions on substrate flexibility - Swiss cheese, weak computational functionalism, constraints on parts, analog computation - all named but not held
